title: Knight Capital 2012: stale code path, deployment split-brain, and automated trading blast radius
summary: Knight Capital is encoded as a software/IT engineering failure in which stale executable logic, deployment inconsistency across servers, weak validation, and non-actionable alerting let a control-plane change create market-scale consequences within minutes.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0010 as part of the first software/IT failure lane.

place.event_context: U.S. equity markets; Knight Capital automated order routing

subjects.name: SMARS automated order routing system / Retail Liquidity Program deployment

claims.claim: The SEC order states that on August 1, 2012 a significant error in Knight Capital’s automated routing system, SMARS, caused millions of orders over about 45 minutes, more than four million executions in 154 stocks, positions involving more than 397 million shares, and losses of more than $460 million.

type_payload.incident_class: financial software deployment and automated trading failure
type_payload.system: SMARS automated routing system, Retail Liquidity Program code deployment, obsolete Power Peg code path, automated monitoring emails

sequence_of_events.event: New RLP-related code was deployed to most but not all production servers.
On the server with old code, a repurposed flag activated obsolete Power Peg behavior.
The system generated continuous child orders at automated-trading speed.
Automated email signals did not become effective operational stop authority before the event became market-scale.

type_payload.proximate_cause: A stale code path was activated through an inconsistent deployment and repurposed flag, causing automated order generation.
